pr.title: Allow unnormalized types in drop elaboration
pr.description:
I work on a [rustc driver](https://github.com/AeneasVerif/charon) that aims to extract the full polymorphic MIR of a crate. Currently the one thing I can't get is drop glue because it fails on unnormalizable types like the fields of `Cow` or `NonZero`.

This PR removes the one check for unnormalized types in drop elaboration. It's a `span_delay_bug` so only there to help catch mistakes. I think that's fine to remove? If something downstream relies on types being normalized the right approach is for MIR validation to check for normalized types, not that one random check.
pr.author: Nadrieril

classification.name: ElaborateDrops
evidence: The patch changes field-type computation inside the drop-elaboration helper used by the concrete `ElaborateDrops` MIR pass. This helper is called while elaborating open ADT drops, so the change directly affects the MIR places constructed by that pass: unnormalized field types are now preserved instead of being replaced with an error type.

analysis.originalLogic: In `compiler/rustc_mir_transform/src/elaborate_drop.rs`, open-ADT drop elaboration computed each field type with `field.ty(tcx, args)` and then forced it through `tcx.try_normalize_erasing_regions(...)`. On `Ok(t)` it used `t`; on `Err(_)` it replaced the field type with `Ty::new_error(...)` and emitted `span_delayed_bug(self.elaborator.body().span, "Error normalizing in drop elaboration.")`. The resulting place was built as `(tcx.mk_place_field(base_place, field_idx, field_ty), subpath)`.
analysis.incorrectTransformation: The historically incorrect transformation was: when normalization of an ADT field type returned `Err` during drop elaboration, replace that field type with an error type and report a delayed bug, instead of retaining the unnormalized `field.ty(tcx, args)`. The corrected transformation computes `let field_ty = field.ty(tcx, args);` and then uses `try_normalize_erasing_regions(...).unwrap_or(field_ty)`, silently preserving the unnormalized type for polymorphic drop elaboration.
analysis.inputDomain: Drop elaboration of open ADT drops in MIR when a field's type cannot be normalized under the elaborator's `TypingMode::PostAnalysis` typing environment, including generic/projection-bearing field types such as those encountered in `Cow` or `NonZero` when extracting polymorphic MIR through rustc internal APIs / a rustc driver.
analysis.summary: Historical bug fix in `ElaborateDrops`: normalization failure for an ADT field type during open drop elaboration was wrongly converted into an error type plus a `span_delayed_bug`. The fix preserves the original unnormalized field type via `unwrap_or(field_ty)`, enabling polymorphic drop elaboration for rustc-internal consumers. The supplied patch contains no regression test changes.
analysis.trigger: `tcx.try_normalize_erasing_regions(self.elaborator.typing_env(), field.ty(tcx, args))` returns `Err` while `ElaborateDrops` is elaborating an open ADT drop.
preconditions: The ElaborateDrops MIR pass is elaborating an open ADT drop and constructing a place field.
The field type comes from `field.ty(tcx, args)` in the current generic/projection context.
The elaborator typing environment is asserted to be `ty::TypingMode::PostAnalysis`.
Normalization of that field type fails in the current typing environment, as with unnormalizable `Cow` or `NonZero` fields.
pitfalls: Treating every normalization failure during drop elaboration as a compiler bug and emitting a delayed bug is too strong for polymorphic use of rustc internal APIs.
Substituting `Ty::new_error` changes the MIR place's field type and can break downstream consumers trying to obtain drop glue or full polymorphic MIR.
The relevant requirement is preserving the original unnormalized type, not dropping normalization entirely when it succeeds.
If downstream code truly requires normalized types, that belongs in MIR validation rather than this single drop-elaboration check, per the PR description.
analysis.testStrategy: Add a focused rustc-driver or MIR-level regression case that elaborates drop glue for a generic ADT whose field type cannot be normalized (e.g. projection-bearing fields like `Cow`/`NonZero`). Compare MIR produced under the two transformations: the corrected path should retain the original unnormalized field type in the drop terminator/place and should not emit the `"Error normalizing in drop elaboration."` delayed bug, whereas the historical path replaces it with an error type and reports the bug. Assert on MIR dumps/diagnostics rather than claiming runtime execution. The supplied patch itself adds no test changes.
